name: The Movielife
label: Revelation
lede: Vinnie Caruana fronted a Long Island band that swapped members with the groups that became Taking Back Sunday, Bayside and Brand New. The Movielife made one record for Revelation that keeps getting repressed, wrecked two vans, and ended in 2003 with a note on its website.

eras.title: Guitarists in, guitarists out
eras.text: The Movielife began in 1997 with Vinnie Caruana singing and a line-up that kept changing. Members left to start bands that grew bigger than the one they left, and by the end of 1999 Caruana had a steady crew, two demos and a debut album on Fadeaway Records.

years.h: Five Long Islanders start The Movielife and cut the Red Demo
years.p: Vinnie Caruana sings, Alex Amiruddin and [[Eddie Reyes|906bf563-38b6-44d0-bb8e-e81f83159ce8]] play guitar, Nick Ghanbarian bass, Evan Baken drums. Producer [[Mike Sapone|96e6e404-ba70-427a-9db9-60019fa6e021]] records the Red Demo.

years.h: Eddie Reyes leaves for Runner Up, then lands in Taking Back Sunday
years.p: His replacement, Dave O'Connell, is gone soon after to form Quick Fix Kills. Reyes, meanwhile, ends up in [[Taking Back Sunday|350bce49-c21b-4137-b50a-0766ded07e4d]].

years.h: Brandon Reilly arrives from the Rookie Lot as Ghanbarian heads to Bayside
years.p: Guitarist [[Brandon Reilly|1016f8b6-7ed0-43e7-ab4d-0b71bb18c342]] comes from Levittown's the Rookie Lot, whose other members went on to form [[Brand New|9311e2bc-bb3f-44cf-90d8-b1fe6912b60b]]. Phil Navetta takes over bass when Ghanbarian leaves for [[Bayside|5f821136-9935-403c-abb5-e78ddda35e9f]].

years.h: The White Demo gets Fadeaway Records interested
years.p: The second demo does the work, and the band signs its first record deal.

years.h: It's Go Time is the debut, out on Fadeaway
years.p: The September release sends the band out on the road, hard.

eras.title: One record for Revelation
eras.text: The Movielife nearly signed with Equal Vision and chose Revelation. This Time Next Year, the one album they made there, is the record fans kept wearing out, and the touring behind it included a van wreck in North Dakota.

years.h: Equal Vision comes close, but Revelation gets the band
years.p: Crowds are growing, and The Movielife have a real choice between two labels. They take the Revelation one.

years.h: This Time Next Year goes to press as Revelation REV 97
years.p: Recorded with [[Brian McTernan|eda2cb2f-b2c6-4e74-9fd7-49ea52df4172]] at Salad Days Studio in Washington, D.C. The first vinyl run is 750 on blue and 900 on black.
years.xp: Demand never went away. Revelation's pressing history lists represses in 2010 (white, red and black), 548 on gold in 2014, 330 on clear in 2015 and 550 on opaque green in 2016.

years.h: A van wreck in North Dakota ends the tour with Bane
years.p: It is February 2001, on a bill with Reach the Sky and [[Bane|adf5ac61-4d7b-4cbc-95ce-ee2dc486f884]]. The Movielife crash the van and have to drop off.

years.h: Glassjaw and New Found Glory in spring, Reel Big Fish by July
years.p: Spring dates with [[Glassjaw|429f9fbf-0a0b-4a9e-a88c-94d48aa466ed]], [[New Found Glory|6acb932e-840d-47ac-8e0d-725ad8a6e52c]] and Autopilot Off give way to the Reel Big Fish and Goldfinger co-headlining run in July and August.

years.h: A September tour with Finch is cancelled after 9/11
years.p: The dates with [[Finch|746737be-e792-42bb-b18c-fb46d7935d7a]] and [[The Starting Line|9701356d-08d9-45ba-975d-977ab466e7be]] never happen after the attacks of September 11.

years.h: Drive-Thru Records picks the band up, and Has a Gambling Problem follows
years.p: The EP lands in November. The year ends on dates supporting [[Good Charlotte|b267ca80-034e-4dc1-9ed4-ec45f1fed41d]] and [[H2O|b4307812-8143-46e0-9075-ffc06b30f3fe]].

eras.title: Forty hours and out
eras.text: The last two years were the busiest: Warped Tour, Europe, a Billboard album and another van crash. Founding guitarist Alex Amiruddin left over the direction of the music, and in September 2003 the band ended with a note on its website.

q: grew disenchanted with the new direction of the music
years.h: Alex Amiruddin quits over the band's new sound
years.p: The founding guitarist leaves for Keep Breathing. Phil Navetta's younger brother Dan takes his place.
years.xp:
Amiruddin said he had grown disenchanted with the direction the music was taking. The Movielife were on Drive-Thru by then, opening for Good Charlotte and the Mighty Mighty Bosstones, and about to spend the summer on Warped Tour.

Amiruddin later joined Wiretap Crash in 2011.

years.h: Europe in the spring, Warped Tour all summer
years.p: The Deconstruction Tour crosses Europe in May and June 2002. From June to August the band is on the Warped Tour.

years.cap: The Movielife at the Kathedral, Toronto, December 13, 2002
years.h: Touring with Brand New puts Reilly next to his old bandmates
years.p: The October to December run takes in The Reunion Show and Orange Island too. Three of Brand New's members once played with Reilly in the Rookie Lot.

years.h: Forty Hour Train Back to Penn peaks at No. 164 on the Billboard 200
years.p: The third album is on Drive-Thru. In May the band shoots a video for Jamestown with Digital Kitchen.
play: Forty Hour Train Back to Penn

years.cap: Bassist and drummer at the Kathedral, Toronto, December 13, 2002
years.h: The van crashes again and Evan Baken is hurt
years.p: The Movielife bring in a fill-in drummer for their UK tour.

years.h: A note on the website ends The Movielife
years.p: After a Hellfest slot and a last run of dates, the split goes up online. The Pitch reported Caruana said goodbye to about 3,000 fans at the farewell show.
years.xp:
Nobody gave a clean reason. Caruana later told Vice that the band was young and "ran into a wall," and that bands break up in the heat of the moment.

Two days after the split, The Pitch reported, Caruana was working demolition on a New York construction site. He also laid tile, and said going back to construction was no good.

eras.title: Two bands, one catalog
eras.text: Caruana and Brandon Reilly split into I Am the Avalanche and Nightmare of You, and Movielife songs kept turning up anyway: acoustic one-offs, a Bamboozle set, then a reunion that came too early.

years.h: A year on, Caruana and Reilly play Movielife songs acoustic
years.p: Caruana is building [[I Am the Avalanche|8e8e27cb-8553-496e-98bc-67bbd72e98dc]] by now, and Reilly fronts [[Nightmare of You|32efc6ae-edf6-4fd1-b268-226073db9a36]].

years.h: At Bamboozle, Set Your Goals are the Movielife
years.p: At the New Jersey festival Caruana sings a set of Movielife songs with [[Set Your Goals|03d8f83e-a647-4bde-968a-189c0f147783]] as his band.

years.cap: The Movielife at Bamboozle, East Rutherford, New Jersey, April 30, 2011
years.h: A YouTube video says The Movielife are playing Bamboozle
years.p: Posted December 16 by Caruana and Reilly. It will be their first show in nearly eight years.

yt: Jamestown at the Bamboozle reunion set
years.h: Bamboozle and a New York show in August, then the reunion stops
years.p: Caruana told Louder neither he nor Reilly was.
years.xp: Caruana's fuller version to Louder: the timing was wrong, and the band was trying to force it.

eras.title: Afraid of drugs, and back for real
eras.text: The second reunion started with two old friends and Reilly's son at a park. It grew into rehearsals three days a week, a return at Irving Plaza, the first new Movielife song in thirteen years and, in 2017, a full album as a trio.

years.cap: Caruana plays acoustic at the Macbeth, Hoxton, London, February 2012
years.h: Three rehearsals a week, with the 2003 line-up back in the room
years.p: Caruana and Reilly reconnect as friends first. Then the Navetta brothers and Baken join in.
years.xp:
Caruana told Louder it began in a park. "We went to the park with his son and we were just playing and hanging out."

Rehearsals followed: "Right now, it's three days a week, which is a lot for us because everyone's got crazy stuff going on."

years.h: Irving Plaza is the comeback
years.p: The first show since 2011 is in New York. UK dates follow in June: London's Electric Ballroom, Birmingham and Manchester.
years.xp: Tickets for the February 7 show went on sale December 19, 2014. Reilly told Vice the money wasn't the point: "none of us need to play a Movielife show. We all have our own careers now."

years.cap: The Movielife at Groezrock, Belgium, April 30, 2016
years.h: After thirteen years, new music arrives with Future Feeling (Afraid of Drugs)
years.p: Vice premieres the song in April.

years.h: A post-election promo photo shows only three Movielife members
years.p: Caruana, Reilly and new drummer Brett Romnes are the whole picture.

years.cap: The Movielife at House of Blues, Anaheim, October 6, 2017
years.h: Fourteen years after the last one, Cities in Search of a Heart
years.p: Out in September on Rise Records, the fourth album. The band plays Slam Dunk Festival in the UK the same year.

years.h: New Found Glory take The Movielife out on the Sick Tour
years.p: US dates in May and June, seventeen years after the two bands first toured together.

years.h: Caruana on more Movielife: ask Reilly
years.p: On the Podioslave podcast Caruana says more music wouldn't surprise him, but Reilly has to write it.
